questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Hydrogen?
questions.explanation: Symbols use the first letter of the element's name, capitalized - H is the lightest element, number 1 on the periodic table.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Helium?
questions.explanation: When the first letter is already taken, a second letter is added in lowercase - He comes from 'Helium' and is the gas that fills party balloons.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Carbon?
questions.explanation: Carbon takes the single letter C - it is the backbone of all living things, and pure carbon forms both soft graphite and hard diamond.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is N, not Ni (that is nickel) - nitrogen gas makes up about 78% of the air you breathe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Oxygen?
questions.explanation: Oxygen is the single letter O - your body uses it to release energy from food, and it makes up about 21% of the air.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Sodium?
questions.explanation: Na does not match the English name because it comes from sodium's Latin name, natrium - watch for these Latin-based symbols on the table.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Magnesium?
questions.explanation: Mg is capital M, small g - capitalization matters in symbols, because MG would mean something completely different. Magnesium burns with a bright white flame.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Aluminum?
questions.explanation: Aluminum is Al - A plus the second letter l, in lowercase. It is the light metal used for cans and foil.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Silicon?
questions.explanation: Si is silicon, the computer-chip element - do not confuse it with S alone (sulfur) or the pair Si written with a capital I, which is not a symbol at all.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Sulfur?
questions.explanation: Sulfur takes the single letter S - a yellow solid famous for its rotten-egg smell near volcanoes and hot springs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Chlorine?
questions.explanation: Cl is C plus a lowercase L (never the number 1) - chlorine is the greenish gas used to kill germs in swimming pools.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Potassium?
questions.explanation: K comes from potassium's Latin name, kalium - the same Latin root that gives us the word 'alkali'. Bananas are a famous potassium source.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Calcium?
questions.explanation: Ca is calcium, the mineral that builds bones and teeth - C alone is carbon, so the second letter a is what makes this a different element.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Iron?
questions.explanation: Fe comes from iron's Latin name, ferrum - that is why iron supplements and the word 'ferrous' start with Fe, not I.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Copper?
questions.explanation: Cu comes from copper's Latin name, cuprum - copper's reddish color and excellent conductivity make it the standard metal for electrical wires.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Zinc?
questions.explanation: Zn pairs Z with n - zinc coats steel buckets and nails (galvanizing) to stop them from rusting.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Silver?
questions.explanation: Ag comes from silver's Latin name, argentum - that is also why Argentina, named for its silver, has the same root.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for Gold?
questions.explanation: Au comes from gold's Latin name, aurum, meaning 'glow of sunrise' - like Fe and Ag, it is a Latin symbol that does not match the English name.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Learn symbols one element at a time.

questions.question: What is an atom?
questions.correctAnswer: The smallest unit of an element that keeps its properties
questions.explanation: Everything is made of atoms, and what makes one element different from another is its atoms: change the number of protons and you have a completely different element.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Atoms are the building blocks.

questions.question: What are the three main parts of an atom?
questions.explanation: Atoms have protons and neutrons in the nucleus and electrons around it.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Protons, neutrons, electrons.

questions.question: What is the charge of a proton?
questions.explanation: The proton's positive charge is exactly equal and opposite to an electron's negative charge, which is why an atom with equal numbers of both is electrically neutral.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Protons are positive.

questions.question: What is the charge of an electron?
questions.explanation: Because electrons carry the negative charge and sit on the outside of the atom, they are the particles that move during electric current and chemical bonding.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Electrons are negative.

questions.question: What is the charge of a neutron?
questions.explanation: With no charge, neutrons are ignored when working out an atom's overall charge - but they still add mass, which is why isotopes of an element have different masses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Neutrons are neutral.

questions.question: Where are protons and neutrons found in an atom?
questions.explanation: Protons and neutrons sit in the dense center, the nucleus.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The nucleus holds protons and neutrons.

questions.question: What is the atomic number of an element?
questions.correctAnswer: The number of protons in its atoms
questions.explanation: The atomic number is the element's ID card: every carbon atom has exactly 6 protons, so atomic number 6 always means carbon, no matter how many neutrons it has.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Atomic number counts protons.

questions.question: What is the mass number of an atom?
questions.explanation: Electrons are left out of the mass number because they are almost 2,000 times lighter than a proton - nearly all of an atom's mass sits in its nucleus.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mass number adds protons and neutrons.

questions.question: What are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons called?
questions.explanation: Isotopes share the same protons but differ in neutrons.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Isotopes differ in neutrons.

questions.question: What is a molecule?
questions.correctAnswer: Two or more atoms bonded together
questions.explanation: Molecules form when atoms bond, like H2O.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Molecules are bonded atoms.

questions.question: What is a compound?
questions.correctAnswer: A substance made of two or more different elements bonded together
distractors: A mix of elements that are not bonded
questions.explanation: Compounds, like water, have elements chemically bonded in a fixed ratio.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Compounds bond different elements.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.explanation: Water is two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Water is H2O.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is one carbon atom bonded to two oxygen atoms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Carbon dioxide is CO2.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for table salt?
questions.explanation: Table salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Salt is NaCl.

questions.question: What is a physical change?
questions.correctAnswer: A change that does not make a new substance
distractors: A change that makes a new substance
questions.explanation: Melting, freezing, and cutting are physical changes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Physical changes keep the substance.

questions.question: Which of these is a physical change?
questions.explanation: Melting changes state but water stays water.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Melting is physical.

questions.question: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Burning makes new substances like ash and smoke.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Burning is chemical.

questions.question: What is a sign that a chemical change has happened?
questions.correctAnswer: A new substance forms, such as gas, color change, or heat
questions.explanation: Signs include gas bubbles, color change, heat, light, or a precipitate.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: New substance means chemical change.

questions.question: In a chemical reaction, what are the starting substances called?
questions.explanation: Reactants are used up and products are made.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Reactants start the reaction.

questions.question: In a chemical reaction, what are the substances made called?
questions.explanation: In a word equation the products go on the right side of the arrow: in 'methane + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water', carbon dioxide and water are the products.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Products are the result.

questions.question: What does the law of conservation of mass say?
questions.correctAnswer: Mass is not created or destroyed in a chemical reaction
questions.explanation: Atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, so mass stays the same.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mass is conserved.

questions.question: What is a balanced chemical equation?
questions.correctAnswer: An equation with the same number of each atom on both sides
distractors: An equation with equal coefficients only
An equation that is always true
questions.explanation: You balance by changing coefficients (the big numbers in front), never the small subscript numbers - changing H2O to H2O2 would change the substance itself, not just its amount.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Balance the atoms.

questions.question: What is the chemical equation for photosynthesis in words?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis also needs sunlight and chlorophyll to run - the glucose stores the Sun's energy, and the oxygen is released into the air as a waste product.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plants make glucose and oxygen.

questions.question: What are the three states of matter?
questions.explanation: The same substance can be all three: water appears as ice (solid), liquid water, and steam (gas) - only the energy and spacing of its particles change.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Solid, liquid, gas.

questions.question: What happens to particles when a solid melts?
questions.correctAnswer: They move faster and farther apart
questions.explanation: Heating adds energy, so particles vibrate faster and break free.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Melting speeds particles up.

questions.question: What is density?
questions.explanation: Density tells you how tightly mass is packed into a space, and its unit mixes both measurements - for example, grams per milliliter (g/mL). Water's density is 1 g/mL, the comparison standard.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Density is mass over volume.

questions.question: An object has mass 60 g and volume 20 mL. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = 60 / 20 = 3 g/mL.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Divide mass by volume.

questions.question: An object has mass 100 g and volume 50 mL. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = 100 / 50 = 2 g/mL.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Divide mass by volume.

questions.question: Will an object with density 0.8 g/mL float in water (density 1 g/mL)?
distractors: It will stay in the middle
questions.explanation: Objects less dense than water float.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Less dense than water floats.

questions.question: Will an object with density 1.5 g/mL float in water?
questions.explanation: Objects denser than water sink.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Denser than water sinks.

questions.question: What is Newton's first law of motion?
questions.correctAnswer: An object stays at rest or in motion unless a force acts on it
distractors: Every action has an equal opposite reaction
questions.explanation: Inertia is an object's resistance to changing its motion, and it grows with mass: a loaded truck is much harder to stop or turn than a bicycle because it has far more inertia.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Inertia keeps things going.

questions.question: What is Newton's second law of motion?
questions.correctAnswer: Force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma)
distractors: Every action has an equal opposite reaction
questions.explanation: A bigger force or a smaller mass gives a bigger acceleration.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: F equals m times a.

questions.question: What is Newton's third law of motion?
questions.correctAnswer: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
questions.explanation: When you push on something, it pushes back just as hard.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Action and reaction are equal.

questions.question: If a force of 10 N acts on a mass of 2 kg, what is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration = force / mass = 10 / 2 = 5 m/s^2.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Divide force by mass.

questions.question: If a force of 20 N acts on a mass of 4 kg, what is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration = 20 / 4 = 5 m/s^2.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Divide force by mass.

questions.question: What is the force on a 3 kg object accelerating at 4 m/s^2?
questions.explanation: Force = 3 x 4 = 12 N.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Multiply mass by acceleration.

questions.question: What is speed?
questions.explanation: The units tell you the formula: speed is measured in distance per time, like meters per second or miles per hour - 'per' is the clue that you divide.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Speed is distance over time.

questions.question: A car travels 120 miles in 2 hours. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = 120 / 2 = 60 mph.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Divide distance by time.

questions.question: A runner covers 400 meters in 50 seconds. What is the speed?
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Divide distance by time.

questions.question: What is velocity?
questions.explanation: That direction makes a real difference: two cars both going 60 mph have the same speed, but if one heads north and the other south, their velocities are different.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Velocity adds direction.

questions.question: What is acceleration?
questions.correctAnswer: A change in velocity over time
questions.explanation: Speeding up, slowing down, or turning are all acceleration.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Acceleration is velocity change.

questions.question: What is kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy depends on mass and speed - and speed counts double: doubling an object's speed gives it four times the kinetic energy, which is why fast crashes are so much more destructive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Moving means kinetic energy.

questions.question: What is potential energy?
questions.explanation: Potential energy is stored, like a ball held high up.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Stored means potential energy.

questions.question: Which object has more kinetic energy: a fast car or a slow car of the same mass?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy grows with speed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Faster means more kinetic energy.

questions.question: What is the unit of energy?
questions.explanation: One joule is a small amount - lifting an apple about one meter uses roughly one joule. Food energy is counted in kilojoules, thousands of joules at a time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Energy is in joules.

questions.question: What is the unit of force?
questions.explanation: The newton is named for Isaac Newton: one newton is about the force of holding a small apple against gravity, and 1 N = 1 kg x m/s^2, straight from F = ma.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Force is in newtons.

questions.question: What is friction?
questions.correctAnswer: A force that opposes motion between surfaces
distractors: A force that speeds things up
questions.explanation: Friction acts against motion, like brakes on a bike.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Friction fights motion.

questions.question: What is gravity?
questions.correctAnswer: A force that pulls objects toward each other
distractors: A force that pushes objects apart
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls objects toward Earth and toward each other.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gravity pulls things together.

questions.question: What is a wave?
questions.correctAnswer: A disturbance that carries energy without carrying matter
questions.explanation: Picture a rope tied to a door: shake your end and the wave travels to the door, but the rope itself stays in your hand - the energy moved, the matter did not.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Waves carry energy.

questions.question: What is the wavelength of a wave?
questions.correctAnswer: The distance between two matching points on a wave
distractors: The number of waves per second
questions.explanation: Wavelength is measured crest to crest or trough to trough.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wavelength is crest to crest.

questions.question: What is the amplitude of a wave?
questions.correctAnswer: The height of a wave from its rest position
distractors: The number of waves per second
questions.explanation: Amplitude is tied to energy: for sound, a bigger amplitude means a louder sound; for light, it means a brighter light - it is measured from the rest position to a crest, not crest to trough.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Amplitude is wave height.

questions.question: What is the frequency of a wave?
questions.correctAnswer: The number of waves that pass a point per second
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Frequency counts waves per second.

questions.question: What is the unit of frequency?
questions.explanation: One hertz means one complete wave passing per second - a sound wave vibrating at 440 Hz completes 440 waves every second, which your ear hears as the musical note A.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Frequency is in hertz.

questions.question: Which type of wave needs a medium to travel?
questions.explanation: Sound needs air, water, or a solid to travel through.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sound needs a medium.

questions.question: Which type of wave can travel through empty space?
questions.explanation: Light is an electromagnetic wave and needs no medium.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Light travels through space.

questions.question: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: That speed is so great that sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth, and light could circle the Earth about 7.5 times in a single second - nothing in the universe travels faster.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Light is super fast.

questions.question: What happens when light hits a mirror?
questions.explanation: Mirrors reflect light, bouncing it off at the same angle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mirrors reflect light.

questions.question: What happens when light passes from air into water?
distractors: It speeds up to light speed
questions.explanation: The bend happens because light changes speed: it slows down entering water, which is why a straw in a glass looks broken or shifted at the surface.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Changing medium bends light.

questions.question: What is an electric current?
questions.explanation: Current is moving charge, usually electrons in a wire.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Current is flowing charge.

questions.question: What is voltage?
questions.correctAnswer: The push that moves electric charge
questions.explanation: Voltage is electric potential difference, the push behind current.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Voltage is the push.

questions.question: What is resistance in a circuit?
questions.correctAnswer: Opposition to the flow of current
questions.explanation: Resistance slows current down and is measured in ohms.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Resistance opposes current.

questions.question: What is the unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: Amps count how much charge flows past a point each second - a phone charger moves about 1-2 amps, while a lightning bolt can carry around 30,000 amps.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Current is in amps.

questions.question: What is the unit of resistance?
questions.explanation: The ohm is named for Georg Ohm: the higher a component's resistance in ohms, the less current a given voltage can push through it - the idea behind Ohm's law, V = I x R.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Resistance is in ohms.

questions.question: What is a series circuit?
questions.correctAnswer: A circuit with one path for current
questions.explanation: That single path has a weakness: if one bulb in a series string burns out, the whole circuit breaks and every bulb goes dark - like old holiday lights.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Series means one path.

questions.question: What is a parallel circuit?
questions.correctAnswer: A circuit with more than one path for current
questions.explanation: Each branch in a parallel circuit gets the full battery voltage, and if one bulb burns out the others stay lit - which is why houses are wired in parallel, not series.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Parallel means many paths.

questions.question: What is a magnet's north pole attracted to?
questions.explanation: Opposite poles attract; like poles repel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Opposites attract.

questions.question: What do two north poles of magnets do?
questions.explanation: You can feel this rule directly: push two north poles together and the magnets shove your hands apart harder the closer they get - that pushing force is repulsion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Like poles push apart.

questions.question: What is thermal energy?
questions.correctAnswer: Energy from the motion of particles
distractors: Energy of motion of a car
questions.explanation: Hotter objects have particles moving faster.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Heat is particle motion.

questions.question: How does heat move by conduction?
questions.explanation: Conduction passes heat when particles bump into neighbors.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Conduction needs contact.

questions.question: How does heat move by convection?
questions.explanation: Convection moves heat in flowing liquids or gases.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Convection flows with fluid.

questions.question: How does heat move by radiation?
questions.correctAnswer: Through electromagnetic waves, no medium needed
questions.explanation: Radiation, like sunlight, travels through space.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Radiation needs no medium.

questions.question: What is the pH of a neutral solution?
questions.explanation: Neutral means the solution is neither acidic nor basic - the scale runs 0 to 14 with 7 in the exact middle, and each step is 10 times stronger than the one before.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Neutral is pH 7.

questions.question: What is the pH range of an acid?
questions.explanation: The lower the number, the stronger the acid: lemon juice is about pH 2 and stomach acid about pH 1, while mild acids like tomato juice sit near pH 4.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Acids are below 7.

questions.question: What is the pH range of a base?
questions.explanation: The higher above 7, the stronger the base: soap is about pH 10 and feels slippery, while drain cleaner reaches pH 14 - strong bases can be as dangerous as strong acids.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bases are above 7.

questions.question: What is a solution?
questions.correctAnswer: A mixture where one substance dissolves evenly in another
questions.explanation: In a solution, the solute dissolves in the solvent.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Solutions dissolve evenly.

questions.question: In salt water, what is the solute?
questions.explanation: The solute is what dissolves; the solvent is what does the dissolving.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Salt is the solute.

questions.question: In salt water, what is the solvent?
questions.explanation: Water dissolves the salt, so water is the solvent.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Water is the solvent.

questions.question: What is the difference between a mixture and a compound?
questions.correctAnswer: A mixture can be separated physically; a compound cannot
distractors: A compound can be separated by filtering
A mixture is always a liquid
questions.explanation: Mixtures keep their own properties and can be separated by physical means.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mixtures separate physically.

questions.question: What is the formula for work?
questions.explanation: Both parts must be present: pushing hard on a wall that does not move does zero work in physics, no matter how tired you get - the force must actually move the object.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Work is force times distance.

questions.question: How much work is done by a 10 N force pushing an object 5 meters?
questions.explanation: Work = 10 x 5 = 50 J.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Multiply force by distance.

questions.question: What is power?
questions.correctAnswer: Work done per unit of time
questions.explanation: Two people can do exactly the same work, but the one who finishes sooner has more power - power is measured in watts, and 746 watts make one horsepower.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Power is work over time.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for lead?
questions.explanation: The symbol for lead is Pb, from its Latin name plumbum.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lead is Pb.
